title: Reject nonterminal task-state collapse to empty snapshot
phase: Twelve Loop Remediation / Orchestrator state integrity

incident.summary: Sequence 1592 of the authoritative task-state journal held 22 nonterminal twelve-loop tasks. Sequence 1593 committed an empty board, superseding all 22 at once; sequences 1594-1595 recovered the catalog by append-only replay.

scope.owned_layer: The task-state journal transition guard in .orchestrator/rewrite/task_state_store.py, its regression suite, the projection verifier live-task count, and the root pytest scrub of inherited task-state environment bindings.
scope.not_changing: Hash-chain and event-digest validation, journal storage layout, .orchestrator/config.json, supervisor dispatch policy, and the ai_status archive/prune flow.

superseded_approach.why_rejected: The count-only rule was merged and then rejected in review because it also refuses the legitimate completion of the final task on the board: the last nonterminal row moving to done drives the nonterminal count to zero without any task being removed.
superseded_approach.replacement: Identity-aware comparison of the previous and new task rows. A commit is refused when task identities that were still live disappear from the board, classified as disappearance when some live identities survive and as mass replacement when none do.

delivered_guard.enforced_before: append_state_commit opens the journal for writing, so a refused commit never reaches the file
fail_closed_rules: A blank, unknown, or unreadable status is treated as live work.
A task row that is not an object, or whose id is missing or blank, is counted as untrackable live work and protected by population comparison.
A tasks container that is not a list hides an unknown amount of live work and is protected the same way.
Dropping the tasks key entirely is treated as removing every live identity.
permitted_without_a_marker: First bootstrap, which has no predecessor identity to preserve.
The final nonterminal task transitioning to a terminal status, because identity is retained.
Archiving rows that were already terminal in the predecessor state, including a fully terminal board draining to empty.

drain_marker.audit_field_contract: reason and actor must be non-empty strings. approved_at must be a non-empty string that parses as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset and is not in the future relative to the commit clock.
drain_marker.task_ids: Must be a list of unique non-empty strings whose stripped set equals exactly the live task ids removed by this commit.
rejected_marker_forms: A marker that is not an object.
A marker missing, blanking, or non-string typing any audit field, including a numeric or boolean reason/actor/approved_at.
A marker whose approved_at does not parse as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or parses without a timezone offset, such as a date-only or naive value.
A marker whose approved_at is in the future, such as 2099-01-01T00:00:00Z.
A marker whose task_ids is not a list of non-empty task id strings.
A marker whose task_ids repeats an id, which inflates apparent coverage without adding evidence.
A marker that names a task still present on the board, which would pre-authorize a future drop.
A marker that does not cover every removed task id.
A marker that names an id that was not a live removal in this commit, such as a never-existing id padded next to the real one.
A marker carried forward byte-identically from the previous commit, which would disable the guard permanently.
A marker without allow_unidentified when rows lacking a task id are removed.
accepted_marker_forms: approved_at as Z, +00:00, a non-UTC offset such as +09:00, or with fractional seconds, provided it is not in the future.
approved_at stamped at commit time by utc_now(), so the not-future rule does not refuse a fresh approval.
task_ids equal to the removed live-id set, including an empty list when the only removal is rows without a task id and allow_unidentified is true.

review_rounds.finding: The declared suites passed and CI was green, but validate_state_transition accepted non-auditable drain markers. With only live task A removed, the guard accepted task_ids [A, NEVER_EXISTED], duplicate task_ids [A, A], approved_at set to a non-timestamp or to the future value 2099-01-01T00:00:00Z, and non-string reason/actor values, because the audit fields were coerced with str(value or '') and the id set was only checked for coverage, not for equality.

remediation.code: _drain_marker_audit_rejection now requires reason, actor, and approved_at to be non-empty str instances; _parse_audit_timestamp requires an ISO 8601 value with an explicit UTC offset and refuses a naive or unparseable one; a parsed approved_at later than datetime.now(timezone.utc) is refused as an approval that was never granted. _drain_marker_ids refuses a repeated id, and the marker id set must now equal the removed live-id set exactly: coverage is still checked first, then any id that was not a live removal in this commit is refused.
tests: test_drain_marker_must_be_explicit_and_audited gained negative cases pads-with-an-id-that-was-never-live, duplicate-task-ids, non-string-task-id, non-string-reason, non-string-actor, non-string-approved-at, unparseable-approved-at, naive-approved-at, date-only-approved-at, and future-approved-at.
test_drain_marker_for_unidentified_rows_must_not_name_phantom_ids covers a padded id on the allow_unidentified path.

The still-legal marker forms are pinned by test_drain_marker_accepts_past_timezone_aware_approvals (Z, +00:00, +09:00, fractional seconds) and test_drain_marker_accepts_an_approval_stamped_at_commit_time, so the not-future rule cannot become a false rejection.

acceptance.criterion: Replay sequence 1592 with 22 tasks followed by an empty state and reject before append
acceptance.proof: .orchestrator/rewrite/test_task_state_store.py::test_incident_replay_rejects_the_empty_snapshot_after_sequence_1592 seeds a hash-chained journal of 1592 events whose head carries 22 nonterminal tasks, asserts the empty commit is refused as a mass replacement, asserts the journal bytes are unchanged and still at sequence 1592, and then commits the recovery board at sequence 1593 linked to the surviving event hash.

acceptance.criterion: Allow first bootstrap and a fully terminal explicitly evidenced drain without weakening hash-chain validation
acceptance.proof: test_allow_first_bootstrap_with_empty_or_no_tasks, test_allow_drain_when_all_previous_tasks_were_terminal, test_completing_and_archiving_the_last_task_stays_possible, test_terminal_rows_may_be_archived_while_live_work_remains, test_audited_drain_marker_authorizes_real_task_removal, test_drain_marker_accepts_past_timezone_aware_approvals, test_drain_marker_accepts_an_approval_stamped_at_commit_time, and test_guard_rejection_does_not_weaken_hash_chain_validation, which shows a journal edited to force the collapse still fails digest validation. The explicitly evidenced drain is only accepted through a marker whose audit fields and id set survive the checks listed under delivered_guard.drain_marker; the sixteen negative cases in test_drain_marker_must_be_explicit_and_audited plus test_drain_marker_for_unidentified_rows_must_not_name_phantom_ids pin the rejected forms. validate_event, the event digest, and the previous-event hash chain are untouched by this task.

acceptance.criterion: Inherited live PANTHEON_TASK_STATE_EVENT_LOG cannot be used by tests or task worktrees
acceptance.proof: conftest.scrub_inherited_task_state_env drops PANTHEON_TASK_STATE_STORE_MODE and PANTHEON_TASK_STATE_EVENT_LOG at pytest_configure and again at pytest_runtest_setup. test_root_conftest_scrubs_an_inherited_live_event_log asserts the scrub contract, test_inherited_live_task_state_env_is_absent_during_tests asserts the resulting process state, and test_task_worktree_pytest_run_cannot_reach_an_inherited_live_event_log runs a child pytest with an authoritative binding exported and asserts the bound journal path is never created. _prepare_parent additionally refuses a relative event log path, which would otherwise mint a private journal inside the task worktree.

acceptance.criterion: Rejected writes leave journal and projection unchanged and parity remains verifiable
acceptance.proof: test_unrelated_workers_not_superseded_and_parity_preserved_after_rejected_drop and the incident replay both compare the journal bytes before and after the refused commit, and scripts/test_verify_task_state_store.py::test_verifier_reports_parity_after_rejected_nonterminal_drop re-runs the verifier after a refused commit and asserts exit 0 with ok true.

acceptance.criterion: Regression covers unrelated workers not being superseded after a rejected empty snapshot
acceptance.proof: test_unrelated_workers_not_superseded_and_parity_preserved_after_rejected_drop projects the journal after the refusal and asserts both task rows keep their in_progress and todo statuses and that the worker records are preserved. test_partial_nonterminal_disappearance_is_rejected covers the single-task variant.

acceptance.criterion: Relevant tests PR checks independent review and merge to dev are required
acceptance.proof: Verification commands below are green locally on the review-round-1 remediation. PR #4224 is open with the three required Branch CI Gate checks green on the previous head; the corrected head returns to Codex2 for independent review, and the merge into dev remains outstanding at the time of this cut.

known_limitations: scripts/ai_status.py prune_archived_active_tasks removes an active row whose id already has an archive snapshot. When such a row is still nonterminal that is a real removal, so the guard now refuses it until the caller supplies an audited drain marker. This repair path is outside this task's artifact scope and is left to a follow-up in ai_status.py; the normal done flow is unaffected because a task row is archived and pruned only after it is already terminal in the predecessor commit.
The drain marker is a store-level contract only. No config, dispatch policy, or status command was changed to emit one.
